text: A clock moves with speed v through inertial frame S. If Δτ is the proper time between two of its ticks, the coordinate time Δt between those ticks measured in S is:
choices: Δt = Δτ / γ, so the moving clock runs fast
Δt = Δτ, because time is absolute
Δt = Δτ / γ², a second-order effect only
Δt = γ Δτ, so the moving clock runs slow
explanation: Time dilation gives Δt = γΔτ with γ = 1/√(1−v²/c²) ≥ 1, so the coordinate time exceeds the proper time — the moving clock runs slow. Choice 1 is the Newtonian assumption of absolute time that SR discards. The proper time Δτ read by the co-moving clock is invariant, while the coordinate time Δt is frame-dependent.
